Pinning the emulated CPU thread to the Thor's prime core (`HAKUX_PLACE_VCPU=prime`) is refuted: it made Crimson Skies slower, so the default does not change. I made no change to `xemu_android.cpp`, and PR #437 is marked ready. CI on the head (49dd45e305) was still pending when I stopped.

**The runs:** six full 480 s runs on the Thor, one binary (15d9406b81), alternating A (normal) and B (pinned). Each run judged 365–369 s of Crimson Skies gameplay and held its full length.

| arm | runs | mean fps |
|---|---|---|
| A (normal) | 28.23, 25.29, 25.07 | 26.20 |
| B (pinned) | 25.56, 18.39, 17.74 | 20.56 (−21.5%) |

The judge failed the prediction on 5 of its checks.

**Why it lost:**
- **Heat took the prime core away.** In B2 and B3, about 240 s into gameplay, the device throttled: the prime core's clock locked at 1843 MHz and the hottest CPU zone dropped from 95 C to 84 C. The pinned thread was then moved onto the slow cores 0–2 for the rest of the run, and gameplay fell to 4–9 fps. No normal run hit that state. My guess is that the pin keeps the prime core busy with no break and so triggers the throttle, but I did not measure that; it happened in 2 of 3 pinned runs.
- **It did not help before that either.** Over the first 240 s, at matched clocks, normal runs averaged 25.8 and pinned runs 24.4. The pin did what it should (the thread went from 70% to 100% of its time on the prime core), but fps did not follow: the pinned thread spent more time waiting for that one core.
- **The expected gain was only an upper bound, and a small one.** Normally the thread already spends 70–80% of its time on the prime core, so the most pinning could save is 2–10% of its time. That is an estimate, not a measured gain, and the extra waiting cost more than that.
- **The pilot's early loss was heat from run order, not the pin.** A2, a normal run after B1, dropped to the same fps once the device was hot.

Because nothing ships, there is no graphics must-not-move run to do. The automatic arms job refused the prediction (both arms use the same build and differ only by an environment variable), so the verdict comes from the lane's own judge script. I posted it on PR #437 and issue #428.

Attempt 1 did not fail. It stopped while hostops reviewed the pilot runs; hostops approved them at 22:31 UTC and this attempt picked up the remaining four. Preflight passes with `--allow-tracker`. Master is merged in and the PR's file list matches the diff. The full tables, run ids and a list of what the next lane should not repeat are in `docs/lanes/vcpuprime428/NOTES.md`. That list includes not pinning to the prime core alone as a default, and comparing runs at matched clocks rather than in run order.
